title: Which quiz group did better?
description: Two groups of different sizes took the same quiz out of one hundred. The mean and the median of each group are found and compared to describe how well each group did.
teaching_notes: One idea: a mean and a median let two groups of different sizes be compared fairly. Watch for children who compare the totals of the two groups instead of their means.

video_script.why: The child can find a mean and a median and now uses both to compare groups.
video_script.substitution: Means and medians allow groups of different sizes to be compared fairly.
video_script.anchor: Marks out of 100 in a general knowledge quiz. First group: 85, 76, 90, 85, 39, 48, 56, 95, 81, 75. Second group: 68, 59, 73, 86, 47, 79, 90, 93, 86.
video_script.payoff_line: The second group did slightly better.

final_answer.value: First group: mean 73, median 78.5; second group: mean ≈ 75.67, median 79; the second group did slightly better
final_answer.spoken: the second group did slightly better

maths_rules: second group sorted: 47, 59, 68, 73, 79, 86, 86, 90, 93; median is the 5th value, 79
the second group is a little higher on both
the low marks 39 and 48 pull the first group's mean below its median
check: first group has 5 marks below 78.5 and 5 above; second group has 4 below 79 and 4 above
video_script.design: Two lists of marks side by side. Each list gets its total and mean first, then is sorted for its median.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Two groups of students took the same quiz, and the marks are out of one hundred.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>One group has ten students and the other has nine.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>How can we compare the two groups fairly?

beats.on_screen: the two lists stay on the board

marks.m1: Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: total ÷ number of marks = mean; a sorted list with its middle mark labelled median

marks.m1: total ÷ number of marks is written and labelled mean
marks.m2: a list sorts itself from least to greatest
marks.m3: the middle mark is labelled median
marks.m4: the hint line the same way as the book's example glows

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The total divided by the number of marks is called the mean.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Sort the marks from least to greatest.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The middle mark of the sorted list is called the median.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>We solve it the same way as the example in your book.

marks.m5: the first five marks of the second list glow
marks.m6: the last four marks of the second list glow

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, the first group has ten marks.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>They are eighty five, seventy six, ninety, eighty five and thirty nine.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The rest are forty eight, fifty six, ninety five, eighty one and seventy five.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The second group has nine marks.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>They are sixty eight, fifty nine, seventy three, eighty six and forty seven.
<bookmark mark='m6'/>The rest are seventy nine, ninety, ninety three and eighty six.

beats.on_screen: To find: mean and median of each group; compare the groups

marks.m1: the questions are written under the lists

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to compare both groups using the mean and the median.

marks.m1: the ten marks are added in a column

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, find the mean of the first group.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The ten marks add up to seven hundred and thirty.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Seven hundred and thirty divided by ten is seventy three.

marks.m1: the nine marks are added in a column

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, find the mean of the second group.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The nine marks add up to six hundred and eighty one.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Six hundred and eighty one divided by nine is about seventy five point six seven.

marks.m2: the fifth and sixth marks of the first list glow
marks.m4: the fifth mark of the second list glows and 79 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, find the median of each group. Sort the marks from least to greatest.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The first group has ten marks, so the median is halfway between the fifth and sixth marks. Those are seventy six and eighty one.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Add them to get one hundred and fifty seven. Half of that is seventy eight point five.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The second group has nine marks, so the median is the fifth mark. It is seventy nine.

beats.on_screen: means 73 and 75.67; medians 78.5 and 79; in the first group the low marks 39 and 48 pull the mean below the median

marks.m1: the two means are written side by side
marks.m2: the two medians are written side by side
marks.m3: 39 and 48 glow in the first list

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, compare the groups. The second group has the greater mean.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>It also has the greater median, but only by a little.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>In the first group, the low marks thirty nine and forty eight pull the mean below the median.

beats.on_screen: check: first group, 5 marks below 78.5 and 5 above; second group, 4 marks below 79 and 4 above

marks.m1: the first sorted list is split at 78.5
marks.m2: the second sorted list is split at 79

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step five, check each median by counting. In the first group, five marks lie below the median and five above.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>In the second group, four marks lie below the fifth mark and four above.

beats.on_screen: Answer: first group mean 73, median 78.5; second group mean ≈ 75.67, median 79; the second group did slightly better
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The second group did slightly better.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The first group has a mean of seventy three and a median of seventy eight point five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The second group has a median of seventy nine. Its mean is about seventy five point six seven.
